text_version.note: AGORA sections of the act only: California AB 1170, SEC. 27-28 (CCPA Amendment 2025); California AB-1170, SEC. 46 (AI in Education Working Group 2025); California AB-1170, SEC. 35 (Generative AI Training Data Documentation 2025)

territorial_scope.description: Applies within California. Civil Code 3111 reaches developers of generative AI systems made publicly available to Californians, and the CCPA definitions apply to businesses doing business in California.

evidence.quote: is made publicly available to Californians for use

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Amends the California Consumer Privacy Act's definitions and rulemaking directions, including on automated decisionmaking, and requires developers of generative AI systems made available to Californians to post training-data documentation by 1 January 2026. Also convenes an education AI working group reporting by 1 January 2027.
summary.long: Sec. 27 and Sec. 28 amend the California Consumer Privacy Act (Civil Code 1798.140 and 1798.185). They revise definitions, including profiling, personal information (which covers inferences and AI systems capable of outputting personal information) and sensitive personal information. They direct the California Privacy Protection Agency to adopt regulations on access and opt-out rights for automated decisionmaking, annual cybersecurity audits and risk assessments for processing presenting significant risk, and opt-out preference signals. Civil and administrative enforcement of the amended provisions may not commence before 1 July 2023. Sec. 46 (Education Code 33328.5) requires the Superintendent to convene an artificial intelligence working group that develops guidance by 1 January 2026, a model policy by 1 July 2026 and a report by 1 January 2027; the section is repealed on 1 January 2031. Sec. 35 (Civil Code 3111) requires developers of generative AI systems released on or after 1 January 2022 and made publicly available to Californians to post training-data documentation on their websites by 1 January 2026 and before each later release or substantial modification. The documentation covers data sources, copyright status, personal and aggregate consumer information, cleaning and synthetic data use. Exemptions cover systems whose sole purpose is security and integrity, aircraft operation in national airspace, and federal national-security or defense uses.

"Business" means:
"Consumer" means a natural person who is a California resident
"Household" means a group, however identified, of consumers who cohabitate with one another at the same residential address

"Personal information" means information that identifies, relates to, describes, is reasonably capable of being associated with, or could reasonably be linked, directly or indirectly, with a particular consumer or household.
For purposes of this paragraph, "publicly available" means any of the following:
"Aggregate consumer information" means information that relates to a group or category of consumers
"Deidentified" means information that cannot reasonably be used to infer information about, or otherwise be linked to, a particular consumer
"Biometric information" means an individual's physiological, biological, or behavioral characteristics
"Sensitive personal information" means:
"Precise geolocation" means any data that is derived from a device
"Profiling" means any form of automated processing of personal information
"Consent" means any freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous indication of the consumer's wishes
"Dark pattern" means a user interface designed or manipulated with the substantial effect of subverting or impairing user autonomy, decisionmaking, or choice, as further defined by regulation.
by the business to a third party for monetary or other valuable consideration
by the business to a third party for cross-context behavioral advertising
"Cross-context behavioral advertising" means the targeting of advertising to a consumer
"Third party" means a person who is not any of the following:
"Service provider" means a person that processes personal information on behalf of a business
"Contractor" means a person to whom the business makes available a consumer's personal information for a business purpose
"Unique identifier" or "unique personal identifier" means a persistent identifier that can be used to recognize a consumer
"Verifiable consumer request" means a request that is made by a consumer
"Research" means scientific analysis, systematic study, and observation
"Artificial intelligence" means an engineered or machine-based system that varies in its level of autonomy
"Local educational agency" means a school district or county office of education.

enforcement.note: The excerpt contains no sanction regime. It amends CCPA definitions (SEC. 27, Civ. Code 1798.140), regulation provisions (SEC. 28, Civ. Code 1798.185) and training-data documentation duties (SEC. 35, Civ. Code 3111), but reproduces no penalty, fine, revocation or injunction provisions. SEC. 28(c)-(d) only defer when enforcement may start ('civil and administrative enforcement ... shall not commence until July 1, 2023') and are not themselves sanctions. The SEC. 46 Education Code section and the SEC. 35 Civil Code section also contain no sanctions.
